title: Password Managers for Android: What to Use and What to Check
html:
On an Android phone you already have a password manager: Google Password Manager. It saves passwords and passkeys to your Google account, fills them in apps and sites, and tells you which ones are exposed or reused. For many people that is enough. A separate app is worth considering only if it fixes a problem you actually have, and you should check who runs it before you hand it every password you own.

Last updated: 10 Oct 2026.

I opened Google Password Manager on a vivo V23 Pro running Android 14 (Funtouch OS 14, security update January 2025) on 10 Oct 2026.

What Google Password Manager does

Google says you can create strong, unique passwords, save them to your Google account, and have them filled in automatically on sites and apps. Its Password Checkup warns you about compromised passwords, and Google says your credentials are protected with encryption, with an optional on-device encryption setting. You can see your passwords at passwords.google.com or in Chrome's password settings.

How to turn saving on or off

Open Settings, search for "Password Manager" and select it, tap Settings at the bottom right, and switch "Offer to save passwords" on or off. In the same place you can turn "Automatically create a passkey to sign in faster" on or off. Google says offering to save passwords and passkeys is on by default.

Check what you have saved

Run Password Checkup. It labels passwords as exposed, weak or used on more than one account. The steps are in our data breach guide. Fix the exposed and reused ones first. For the accounts that matter most (email, banking), also turn on a second step: see two-factor authentication explained.

If you want a different password manager

Android lets you choose which service fills your passwords; search "Autofill service" in Settings. Before you move, check these about any manager:

  • Who runs it, and how it makes money.
  • How it protects your vault. Read its own security page, and whether it has been independently reviewed.
  • What happens if you lose your phone or forget the master password. Some managers cannot recover a vault.
  • Whether you can export your passwords, so you are not locked in.
  • Which permissions the app asks for on your phone. See our permissions guide.

Password managers tried, with results

I use Google Password Manager on my vivo V23 Pro. The home screen has three tabs at the bottom: Accounts, Checkup and Settings. Under Accounts you can filter by All, Passwords, Passkeys and Network devices, and there is an Add password button above the list. On my phone it also showed a banner saying "For added safety, encrypt your passwords on your device before they're saved to Google Password Manager", with Dismiss and Set up buttons. I have not used any other password manager, so I am not comparing them from experience; the other apps in this post are described from their own pages.

What to do next

  1. Open Password Manager in Settings and make sure saving is on.
  2. Run Password Checkup and change the exposed and reused passwords.
  3. Turn on 2-step verification for your email and bank accounts.
